description: Graph-native quantum-grain flood/route/explore/refine over SpaceQuantum belief (dynamic, foveated, N-dimensional quanta navigation -- CLAUDE.md's Rust-is-the-agent split: this seed is graph DATA only, no Python decisions). qf_seed_goal/qf_seed_frontier seed the Bellman flood root(s) (single committed goal, or multi-source over every frontier quantum while exploring); qf_relax propagates qdist=distance-to-goal backward over portal edges gated by oneway_ok; qf_visit marks the avatar's containing quantum visited; qf_hop_direct/qf_hop_route are the ONE decision writing game.chosen_action (per-dim sign step when the goal shares the avatar's box, else Argmin-portal descent over a pool FILTERED by oneway_ok+freshness, clamped to the crossing span), mapping the desired displacement to the world's action vocabulary via the EXISTING is_self-region responds_via/ControlResponse Dot-pick (no hardcoded Up/Down/Left/Right, N-dim by construction); qf_frontier_goal commits the nearest frontier (Argmin, deterministic tiebreak -- exactly one mint per cycle, not one per tied frontier) as a uniform Goal{pose,exploration,commit_epoch} node; qf_goal_retire is the ONLY rule that removes a committed_goal, and only an exploration-minted one (reached / no-longer-frontier / superseded by a fresher one) -- world-committed goals are never touched; qf_stale_on_belief_change/_block_interior/_block_portal turn an observed belief correction or blocked crossing into either a per-dim stale mark (resplit) or a flipped portal oneway_ok; qf_requantize_flag is the adapter's epoch-gated cue to re-run space_quantize; qf_closed/qf_mint_hyp port msp_closed/msp_mint_hyp to quantum grain (movement exhausted -> a non-movement-affordance Hypothesis). All qf_* rules guard on game.nav_repr=="quanta"; hop_descend_gradient (cell mode, seeds/grid_navigation.json) is untouched and starves naturally in quanta mode since _dist is never written there.

microtheory.name: quanta_navigation
microtheory.description: quantum-grain flood/route/explore/refine over SpaceQuantum belief, body-conditional and foveated

rules.name: qf_seed_goal
rules.comment: a WORLD-committed goal's containing quantum -> qdist=0 (single-source flood root). Restricted to `world==1` goals ONLY (not exploration-minted ones): an exploration goal's own quantum is ALREADY a flood source via qf_seed_frontier (it's one of the frontiers) -- seeding it AGAIN here would be redundant while fresh and actively HARMFUL once stale (a churned exploration-goal pose that no longer sits in a frontier would otherwise plant a bogus single-source root at an arbitrary already-explored cell, competing with the real multi-source frontier flood qf_hop_route/qf_frontier_goal depend on).

rules.name: qf_seed_frontier
rules.comment: no WORLD-committed goal (pure exploration) -> every frontier quantum is a flood source (multi-source qdist=0); qf_frontier_goal separately commits ONE of them as a bookkeeping Goal{pose} (for qf_hop_direct's exact-arrival step + other consumers), but that exploration goal does NOT gate this rule off (guard is world==1 specifically, not 'any committed_goal') -- the multi-source flood stays live across every known frontier the whole time exploration is active, so hop can still route toward WHICHEVER frontier is nearer via the CURRENTLY known portal graph even if the nominally-committed one turns out to be unreached / disconnected so far. This is what makes aggressive goal retiring unnecessary for correctness (qf_goal_retire is now a lifecycle/bookkeeping cleanup, not a routing necessity).

rules.name: qf_relax
rules.comment: Bellman relax: Q.qdist <- min(Q.qdist, R.qdist+cost) over portal Q->R with oneway_ok. Batched -- bindings snapshotted before mutation, converges via set_attr_if_different's own progress flag.

rules.name: qf_hop_direct
rules.comment: goal is inside the avatar's own quantum -> per-dim sign step straight to it (a passable box admits any interior motion by construction, no per-cell flood needed).

rules.name: qf_hop_route
rules.comment: goal not in the avatar's own quantum (or exploring) -> pick the portal minimising (neighbour qdist + cost) from the FILTERED candidate pool (oneway_ok==1 AND target qdist fresh this epoch -- filtered into the Argmin pool itself, not just guarded), then step: crossing dim follows the portal's dir (gated in-span on the other dims), other dims clamp toward the shared span.

rules.name: qf_frontier_goal
rules.comment: commits the SINGLE nearest frontier (Argmin, deterministic first-encountered tiebreak) by matching F against that one winner -- NOT 'any frontier tied at the min qdist', which used to commit every tied frontier as its own Goal in the same pass.

rules.name: qf_goal_retire
rules.comment: retires an exploration-minted committed_goal when reached (avatar pose == goal pose exactly), its pose is no longer covered by any frontier quantum (resolved by observation/decode), or a fresher exploration goal superseded it. World-committed goals (`world==1`) are never touched -- only ever `exploration==1` goals.

rules.name: qf_stale_on_belief_change
rules.comment: a belief-correction observation (game -belief_changed-> BC{pose,dim}, mechanical adapter stamp) inside a quantum's box -> mark it stale for a per-dim resplit. Same stale/stale_dim/stale_pose contract as qf_stale_on_block_interior; the adapter no longer scans quanta for containment itself.

rules.name: qf_stale_on_block_interior
rules.comment: block observation strictly inside a quantum's box (not on a face along the blocked dim) -> a mover/obstacle appeared mid-box; mark stale for a per-dim resplit.

rules.name: qf_stale_on_block_portal
rules.comment: block observation on a quantum's face, matching an existing portal's crossing dim/dir -> flip that portal's oneway_ok (no split needed).

rules.name: qf_closed
rules.comment: avatar's own quantum never got a qdist this epoch, though something was seeded (goal committed or a frontier exists) -> movement exhausted.

rules.name: qf_mint_hyp
rules.comment: add_node_if_absent (not add_node) so a same-pass double-binding of Q (irrelevant to the effect, just along for the match) can't mint two Hypotheses -- the dedup key IS the kind, matching msp_mint_hyp's single-hypothesis intent exactly.
